title: Against Celsus, Book VII
blurb: Celsus ranks the oracles of Apollo above the Hebrew prophets, claims that Moses and Jesus taught opposite laws, and tells Christians to seek God through Plato and to honour the gods and demons with altars and images. Origen answers that the prophets spoke by the Spirit of God and foretold Christ, that the law and the Gospel agree when read in the spirit, that God is known by a mind made in His image, and that Christians may serve no demon and worship no image.
first_english_note: Earlier English: Frederick Crombie (Ante-Nicene Fathers, 1872) and Henry Chadwick (1953). This is a fresh English translation from Koetschau's Greek; neither was used as wording.

text_history.method: Translated from the Greek of Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI, which serves as the copy-text. Each chapter was translated from the Greek and then checked clause by clause against it in an independent review. No earlier English translation was consulted.
